Why does the preceptor teach the five meditation themes at ordination?

The text explains: *"Yet such honor and fame hardly touched him inwardly: at heart he always remained a simple monk whose greatest joy was quiet study and meditation at his small village temple near the town of Balangoda."* The five themes — hair of head (kesā), hair of body (lomā), nails (nakhā), teeth (dantā), skin (taco) — are not arbitrary. They target the root of infatuation with the body. The skin, as the outermost layer, is what we are actually attracted to when we conceive of a body as beautiful. Contemplating the skin as a wrapping that holds together otherwise repulsive components directly undercuts sensual desire. This is the very first teaching given to a new monk — showing that the entire path begins with honest, unflinching investigation of the body.
